This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
is one step of writing a scene: plan, write, revise. It ends with a **Do
it** task on your own scene and one set of questions. The full
explanations, examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary scene-card scene-turn character-voice scene-heading action-line dialogue subtext story-beat protagonist conflict >}}

## 8.1 Plan before you write: the scene card

- A **scene card** plans one scene: place and time, characters, goal,
  obstacle, **turn**, beat, length.
- The **turn** is the change near the end that moves the story on.
- The **beat** says where the scene sits in the stages of the game (the
  beat table of lecture 4).
- "Rooftop": EXT. ROOFTOP – NIGHT. Nour (17) and Grandma Salma (78). Goal:
  Nour wants Salma in the boat now. Obstacle: Salma will not leave her
  house of fifty years. Turn: the water opens the door; Salma gives Nour the
  house key and gets in. Beat: end of stage 1, the first family is safe.
  Length: about 30 seconds.
- Order: the street scene → "Rooftop" → the market. Nour cannot go on while
  Salma is still on her roof.

![The scene card of "Rooftop".](images/scene-card.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"Nour talks to Salma" is not a turn. Ask: what is different at the end?
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Your scene card"}
Choose one scene of your premise from lecture 6 (or of a game you know).
Write its card: place and time, characters, goal, obstacle, turn, beat,
length. Does the turn change something for the next scene?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · The scene card"}
Use the card of "Rooftop" above. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the market|Captain Tarek"}
What is Nour's goal?
:   Salma in the boat now

What is the obstacle?
:   Salma will not leave her house

What is the turn?
:   Salma gives Nour the key and gets in

Which scene comes just before "Rooftop"?
:   the street scene

"Nour talks to Salma on the roof." What is missing on this card?
:   a turn: nothing changes
:::
:::

## 8.2 Write it: action first, then voices

- **Start late:** begin when the problem is already there (Salma refuses).
  Skip the greetings.
- **Action lines first:** the rain, the rising water, the door. The player
  sees more than the characters say.
- **One voice per character:** the words, the length of the sentences, the
  tone.
- "We must leave now" in three voices: Nour "Get in. Now." · Salma "My
  child, a house is only walls. Let us go." · Captain Tarek "All boats,
  leave sector four now. Over."
- **Cover the names:** can you still tell who speaks?

![Three characters, three voices.](images/voices.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
If all characters use the same words and long sentences, they all sound like
the writer.
:::

{{< sim file="sims/voice-match.html" poster="sims/voice-match.png" title="Voice Match: who says this line?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Write your draft"}
Play **Voice Match**. Then, in Word, write the first draft of the scene on
your card: the heading, two or three action lines and six to ten lines of
dialogue, in the format of lecture 7.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Voices"}
Nour: short orders. Salma: slow, old sayings, "my child". Tarek: formal,
numbers, "Over". Who says it? You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="the narrator"}
"Two more roofs. Then the hill."
:   Nour

"In my day, we built our houses on stone."
:   Salma

"Boat three, report your position. Over."
:   Tarek

"Leave the photos. We'll come back for them."
:   Nour

"Come, sit with me a while, child."
:   Salma
:::
:::

## 8.3 Revise: read it aloud, then cut

- Read the scene **aloud**: the ear finds what the eye misses.
- **Cut** every line that does no job. Keep the goal, the obstacle and the
  turn.
- Checklist: Does something change? Can a line be cut? No "as you know" and
  no small talk? Feelings shown, not named? A voice for each character? The
  format right? Does it fit its beat and its length?
- "Rooftop" draft: 52 seconds. Cut the small talk (7 s), the "as you know"
  line and its answer (8 s), "I am very scared and very sad" (3 s):
  52 − 18 = **34 seconds**.

![Revise: read it aloud, then cut.](images/revise.png){width=92%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Never cut the turn ("Lock it for me."). A short scene without its turn is
worse than a long one.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Revise your draft"}
Read your draft aloud. Go through the checklist. Cut at least two lines, and
fix one line so that it shows a feeling instead of naming it.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Cut or keep?"}
The draft of "Rooftop" must be 35 seconds at most. Cut or keep each line?
You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="move it to the start"}
SALMA: "Hello, Nour. How is your mother?"
:   cut: small talk

NOUR: "As you know, the river has flooded the whole old city."
:   cut: "as you know"

SALMA: "Lock it for me."
:   keep: it is the turn

SALMA: "I am not going. Fifty years I have lived in this house."
:   keep: it is the obstacle

NOUR: "I am very scared and very sad."
:   cut: it names the feeling
:::
:::

## Game challenge: the Night Owl table read {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

At *Night Owl Games*, the writers read their scenes aloud around a table.
The producer listens with a stopwatch. The first draft of "Rooftop" runs
**52 seconds**; it must be **35 seconds at most**, with the goal, the
obstacle and the turn kept. It has small talk ("How is your mother?", 3 s,
and "She's fine…", 4 s), an "as you know" line (5 s) with its answer (3 s),
and a line that names a feeling ("I am very scared and very sad", 3 s).

{{< sim file="sims/scene-cutter.html" poster="sims/scene-cutter.png" title="Scene Cutter: cut the scene to its length" kind="game" height="820" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · The table read"}
"Rooftop": first draft 52 seconds, at most 35. Weak lines: small talk 3 s +
4 s, "as you know" 5 s and its answer 3 s, the named feeling 3 s. Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="52 seconds|30 minutes"}
How long is the scene after all five weak lines are cut?
:   34 seconds

Is that short enough for the producer?
:   yes, 35 seconds at most

Which part of the card must never be cut?
:   the turn

Why does the producer want a short cutscene?
:   players skip long cutscenes
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Fix the scene (harder)"}
"Rooftop", EXT. ROOFTOP – NIGHT. Nour: short orders. Salma: slow, old
sayings. Choose the better version of each line.

::: {.match extra="Salma is very angry."}
Nour, in a hurry, tells Salma to get in.
:   "Get in. Now."

Salma shows that she is afraid, without saying it.
:   "That door has never opened by itself."

An action line that the camera can film.
:   The water reaches the door below.

Salma agrees in her own voice.
:   "My child, a house is only walls. Let us go."
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Plan a scene on a card: place and time, characters, goal, obstacle, turn, beat, length.
- The beat places the scene in the stages of the game; the turn opens the next scene.
- Start late, write the action lines first, and give each character a voice.
- Read the draft aloud, then cut the lines that do no job.
- Never cut the goal, the obstacle or the turn.
